issues.claim: Подумайте, как внимательно человек читает дифф на 2000 строк и что придётся делать, если такое изменение сломает production.
issues.problem: The hint nearly restates two of the three claims in the correct option (thoroughness of review, rollback). It is still a nudge, but it is close to giving the answer away. The same applies to the English hint.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten the hint to something like "Подумайте, что удобнее ревьюеру и что проще, если изменение придётся отменить." and update the en hint to match. Alternatively keep it as is.

issues.claim: Набор меток стоит договорить в команде.
issues.problem: "договорить" is unnatural Russian in this context. It does not mean "agree on".
issues.suggestedFix: Набор меток стоит согласовать в команде.

issues.claim: Make the review outcome explicit. For example, approve the change with the remaining minor comments when only those are left, so the author does not wait for a second round.
issues.problem: "LGTM with comments" is described on speed.html, which is not linked here. The excerpt of standard.html supports only the weaker point, that reviewers should favour approving an imperfect CL and prefix unimportant remarks with "Nit:". The claim is correct in general but is not directly backed by the cited pages.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add https://google.github.io/eng-practices/review/reviewer/speed.html to links (with linkTitles in both locales) or soften the bullet to say that minor remaining remarks, marked Nit, should not hold up approval.

issues.claim: Usually they either treat every comment as required and spend time on trivia, or start skipping all of them, including the important ones.
issues.problem: The comments page supports only the first half (authors may read all comments as mandatory). The second half, skipping everything, is the generator's own speculation. The same applies to the ru text.
issues.suggestedFix: Say "authors may treat every comment as mandatory, even those meant as optional or informational" and drop or soften the claim that they skip all comments.
